summary_paragraph: Ms. ___ was admitted due to concerns about delirium and inability to care for herself, following an episode where she locked herself in the bathroom, refused medications, and exhibited confusion. Upon evaluation, her mental status improved and was determined to be secondary to dehydration rather than primary psychosis. Her creatinine was elevated at 2.8, consistent with acute kidney injury in the setting of prerenal dehydration, which resolved with IV fluid rehydration. She remained in normal sinus rhythm, with stable heart function and no signs of acute pulmonary disease. Dry gangrene of the toes was noted, but vascular surgery advised outpatient follow-up without urgent intervention. A care plan was established involving her grandson and home health services to support medication management and activities of daily living, respecting her autonomy. She was discharged home with services on a reduced dose of furosemide, with instructions to monitor weight and follow up with her PCP and vascular surgery.
